LanguageData.PF_Text_071: The first apprentice practiced sharpening long after the forge went dark. The ripples left on the blade resembled dying flames. Each successor would later carve a personal mark at its base.
LanguageData.PF_Text_072: This axe was first made to break open the damaged gate of a caravan stop. Its short rear beak reached the jammed bolt, giving the smith a tool that would later prove useful against walls.
LanguageData.PF_Text_073: After a mechanoid raid, the second apprentice filled the workshop manual with sketches of joints in broken armor. Notes on weak points led to this design, combining a broad hammer face with a long pick.
LanguageData.PF_Text_074: Caravan sentries asked for many revisions to their spearheads. The final winged design accompanied them through snow and wasteland; its pointed butt helped steady their footing on loose slopes.
